newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Montell turns to profit in Q4 1996 as margins rise.
newsitem.headline: Montell turns to profit in Q4 1996 as margins rise.

text.p: Montell Polyolefins said on Friday a recovery of polyolefin margins had turned a 1995 fourth quarter loss of $123 million into a 1996 fourth quarter profit of $92 million.
"In 1996 the polypropylene market recovered from its sharp downturn during the second half of 1995," the company said in a statement.

However, while revenues rose by $89 million, or 9.5 percent, from the third quarter, the operating result fell by nine percent due to lower results in olefins and polyolefins and additional restructuring costs.
The company was upbeat on future prospects.
"We expect to achieve additional benefits and productivity improvements during 1997 and 1998 which will strengthen our competitive position," said chief executive officer Peter Vogtlaender.
He added that the company's healthy cash flow position should enable it to achieve all their "ambitious investment program" even if margins come under pressure.
Montell is a plastics joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell and Italy's Montedison.
